images.title: Pencil and school bag against 1 kg
images.purpose: Show that a pencil is lighter than the 1 kg block and a school bag is heavier, and that 1 kg is 1,000 g, so grams are for light things and kilograms for heavy things.
images.composition: A banner with the rule at the top and two balances below, a pencil against the 1 kg block on the left and a school bag against the 1 kg block on the right.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. TWO BALANCES side by side, each a two pan balance. Balance 1 is centred at x 364: a vertical post 12 px wide from y 320 to y 600 in grey #6B7280 on a base 200 by 24 px at y 600 to 624; a beam 360 px long and 12 px thick tilted so that its right end is lower (rotated 8 degrees clockwise about the top of the post at (364, 320)), dark #1F2937; two pans, each a half ellipse 120 px wide hung by two thin lines from a beam end. On the HIGHER left pan of balance 1 sits a pencil: a long thin rectangle 110 by 14 px filled amber #E69F00 with a pink end 16 px wide and a dark tip. On the LOWER right pan sits a 1 kg block: a square 70 by 70 px filled teal #0072B2 with the text 1 kg in white (32 px, bold). Balance 2 is centred at x 1092 and is built the same way, tilted the other way: its left end is lower (rotated 8 degrees anticlockwise). On the LOWER left pan sits a school bag: a rounded rectangle 90 by 100 px filled reddish purple #CC79A7 with a small handle arc and a front pocket 56 by 36 px. On the HIGHER right pan sits the same 1 kg block, 70 by 70 px, teal #0072B2 with the text 1 kg. TAGS: under balance 1, centred at x 364 and y 690, the tag Pencil 6 g; under balance 2, centred at x 1092 and y 690, the tag School bag 4 kg (each a rounded rectangle 280 by 56 px filled very pale grey #F3F4F6 with a 3 px outline #6B7280, text dark #1F2937, 36 px, bold). RULE BANNER centred at x 728 and y 120: the text 1 kg = 1,000 g (60 px, bold, dark #1F2937) inside a rounded rectangle 560 by 96 px with a 4 px outline #0072B2. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any count of balances, pans or blocks that differs from 2 balances, 4 pans and 2 blocks
a balance tilted the wrong way (the pencil side must be higher, the school bag side lower)
any weight or text other than the four labels listed
images.takeaway: A pencil is lighter than 1 kg, so it is weighed in grams; a school bag is heavier than 1 kg, so it is weighed in kilograms.
images.description: Two balances: a pencil against a 1 kg block, and a school bag against a 1 kg block, with 1 kg = 1,000 g.
images.context: Concept image for Gram or Kilogram? It follows the idea of the figures in your maths book (weighing things against a 1 kg weight) and shows the concept's own example of a pencil and a school bag (practice values).
images.teaching_notes: Ask which side goes down on each balance and why. The slip to watch: reading 6 g and 6 kg as nearly the same weight.

image_decisions.why: The two tilted balances show which thing is lighter and which is heavier than 1 kg, and the banner links the two units.
